The retrieved cases only show very weak, non-specific answers ('yes', 'no', 'abscess') and do not strongly match this anatomy or question, so they should not be treated as indicative of the current image.

key_facts: Normal brain MRI should show symmetric cerebral hemispheres and midline alignment of the falx and corpus callosum.
The lateral ventricles should be appropriately sized and symmetric, without hydrocephalus or mass effect.
Cortical sulci and deep white matter should not show abnormal enlargement, edema, or focal lesions.
Incidental findings on brain MRI may include benign cysts, mild chronic small-vessel white matter change, or developmental variants.
Any focal signal abnormality, enhancement, or distortion of midline structures may indicate a pathologic process rather than an incidental variant.
